issues.detail: Covers only the happy path of building a guide and gives no handling for missing brand info, an existing brand to preserve, conflicting inputs, or a palette that fails contrast checks.
Steps produce markdown templates with bracketed placeholders but no runnable commands, contrast-checking script, or concrete procedure for generating tints/shades or exporting the guide.

scenarios.name: fintech-brand-guide-accessible-colors
scenarios.rationale: Both supply primary, neutral, semantic colors with hex values, contrast tables flagging white/green failures with Deep Green alternatives, a type scale, and design guidance; A has a dedicated Do's and Don'ts table (explicitly required) and a more complete type scale with a 'Fail' flag plus a safer alternative, while B lacks a formal Do's/Don'ts section (only logo don'ts and a checklist), uses approximate ratios, and omits the white-on-green pairing explicitly, though it has more semantic detail and tokens.

scenarios.name: developer-tool-color-palette-with-tints
scenarios.rationale: Response B covers the rubric nearly point by point: a tint/shade primary scale with hover/pressed roles, a neutral scale mapped to roles, semantic colors, contrast tables, and an explicit large-text-only case (white on #3b82f6 at 3.7:1) with a darker button fill recommended. Response A has only a single primary pair with hover, a thinner neutral set, and no explicit large-text-only identification.

scenarios.name: voice-and-tone-plus-logo-rules
scenarios.rationale: Both cover traits with examples, a tone table, writing rules, logo variants, clear space, and don'ts; A includes the explicit wordmark-only variant, an explicit 25-word sentence limit, and a social media tone row, while B has 4 traits, omits the wordmark-only variant (uses stacked instead), and lacks a social media row in the tone table (though it mentions social emoji in rules) but adds extra useful sections.
